blocks.prompt: 9. Write the equation \(\arg(\overline{z} - 2 + i) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) in cartesian form, if \(z = x + iy\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh 'locus' ka sawal hai. Locus (points ka raasta) ka matlab hai: woh tamam points jo ek shart poori karte hain. Yahan shart argument ki shakal mein di gayi hai, aur humein use x aur y wali aam equation (cartesian form) mein badalna hai. Plan: \(\overline{z} - 2 + i\) ko (real part) + (imaginary part)i mein likhein, phir \(\tan\theta = \frac{\text{imaginary}}{\text{real}}\) lagayein, aur aakhir mein quadrant ki shart na bhoolein, kyunke tan ek hi value do ulti directions ko deta hai.
steps:
Given (diya gaya hai): \(z = x + iy\) aur \(\arg(\overline{z} - 2 + i) = \frac{2\pi}{3}\).
To find (maloom karna hai): x aur y mein equation (cartesian form).
Method (tareeqa): agar \(\arg(a + ib) = \theta\) ho to \(\tan\theta = b/a\), aur point \((a, b)\) usi quadrant mein hona chahiye jis mein \(\theta\) hai.

Qadam 1: Number ko a + ib form mein likhein
\[\overline{z} = x - iy\]
\[\overline{z} - 2 + i = (x - 2) + (1 - y)i\]
Kyun: conjugate (jora: imaginary part ka sign ulat dena) se \(\overline{z} = x - iy\). Phir real hisse \((x - 2)\) aur imaginary hisse \((-y + 1)\) alag alag ikatthe kiye.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(z\) nahi, \(\overline{z}\) hai. Agar \(z\) le liya to imaginary part \(y + 1\) ban jayega aur poora jawab badal jayega.

Qadam 2: Argument ka tan lagayein
\[\tan\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{1 - y}{x - 2}\]
\[\tan\dfrac{2\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}\]
\[\dfrac{1 - y}{x - 2} = -\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(a + ib\) ka argument \(\theta\) ho to \(\tan\theta = b/a\). \(\frac{2\pi}{3} = 120^{\circ}\) second quadrant mein hai jahan tan negative hota hai: \(\tan 120^{\circ} = -\tan 60^{\circ} = -\sqrt{3}\).

Qadam 3: y ko akela karein
\[1 - y = -\sqrt{3}(x - 2)\]
\[1 - y = -\sqrt{3}x + 2\sqrt{3}\]
\[y = \sqrt{3}x - 2\sqrt{3} + 1\]
Kyun: pehle cross-multiply kiya (\(x - 2\) ko doosri taraf zarb), phir bracket khola, phir \(y\) ko ek taraf aur baqi sab doosri taraf. Yeh ek seedhi line ki equation hai jis ka slope \(\sqrt{3}\) hai.

Qadam 4: Quadrant ki shart
Angle \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) second quadrant mein hai, is liye real part \(x - 2 < 0\) aur imaginary part \(1 - y > 0\), yani \(x < 2\).
Kyun: \(\tan\theta = -\sqrt{3}\) angle \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) (fourth quadrant) ke liye bhi sach hai. Line ka woh aadha hissa argument \(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) ka hai, \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) ka nahi. Is liye locus line ka sirf woh hissa hai jahan \(x < 2\): yeh ek ray hai jo \((2, 1)\) se shuru hoti hai (yeh point khud shaamil nahi, kyunke wahan number 0 ban jata hai jis ka argument hota hi nahi).
Dhyan dein: zyada tar students yahan ruk jaate hain aur poori line likh dete hain. Poori line likhna aam taur par qabool hai, lekin samajhna zaroori hai ke asal mein aadhi line hi sahi hai.

Tasdeeq (check): \(x = 1\) lein; line se \(y = 1 - \sqrt{3}\).
\[\overline{z} - 2 + i = (1 - 2) + (1 - 1 + \sqrt{3})i\]
\[= -1 + \sqrt{3}\,i\]
Yeh point second quadrant mein hai aur \(\tan\theta = -\sqrt{3}\), is liye \(\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}\). Sahi.
blocks.final_answer: \(y = \sqrt{3}x - 2\sqrt{3} + 1\) (sirf woh hissa jahan \(x < 2\)): \((2, 1)\) se baayein taraf jaane wali ek seedhi ray.
